newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand gets biggest ever yen loan from Japan.
newsitem.headline: Thailand gets biggest ever yen loan from Japan.

text.p: Thailand on Friday signed its largest-ever loan agreement with Japan to finance infrastructure, health care and environmental development projects, the Japanese embassy said.

The 118.38 billion yen loan agreement was signed by Thai finance ministry and Japan foreign ministry representatives, and repreented a 92 percent increase over a loan granted to Thailand by Japan last year, it added in a statement.
The 25-year loan package will have interest rates of between 2.3 percent and 2.7 percent per year with a seven-year grace period, it said.

The projects to be financed include the second Bangkok International Airport development which will get 31.22 billion yen in loans and a subway mass transit project which was awarded a loan of 26.59 billion yen, the embassy said.
A 16.61 billion yen loan will finance the construction of the second stage of a new expressway project in the northern suburbs of Bangkok, the statement said.
"The Government of Japan will...continue to contribute to the socio-economic advancement of Thailand by means of Official Development Assistance in the years to come," the embassy statement said.
